summary: Fence newly terminal schedule owners while preserving existing duties

replay.detail: No projection or replay changes. Stops and diagnostics use existing claim kinds.

schema.detail: No table migration or claim-field registry change. Daemon startup persists a local schedule_owner_guard_epoch_v1 marker. Newly terminal run/step lifecycle source claims carry a top-level schedule_owner_guard_epoch annotation in the existing opaque claim body, including terminal work and carried-step records. Schedule owner views add owner-terminal status and legacy-leftover metadata.

rules.detail: New cancellation cleanup stops owned intake by exact subject identity before waiting on unresolved effects. Arming, timer dispatch and queued-work admission enforce terminal ownership only when the source terminal transition carries the new lifetime epoch. Unstamped terminal owners retain their existing schedules, including history imported after upgrade. Reasserting an already-terminal state preserves its original policy.

compatibility.detail: No automatic stop of existing schedules with pre-upgrade terminal owners. These legacy leftovers keep firing and are reported as owner-terminal for manual migration. Owners that transition to terminal under an upgraded daemon are lifetime-bounded; step-owned schedules do not outlive newly completed, failed, cancelled or skipped steps. Unowned schedules and already-started scheduled mission runs are unchanged.

downtime.detail: No data migration or downtime. The durable epoch is enabled once when the updated daemon starts and survives restart/reopen. Enforcement follows source annotations, not wall-clock ordering or replication arrival time.

manual.detail: Use schedules ls/show to find owner-terminal legacy leftovers. For a duty intended to survive its creator, publish an independent schedule without run/step ownership, verify its host, cadence and mission/workspace, then explicitly stop the old owned schedule to avoid duplicate work. For obsolete duties, explicitly stop the legacy schedule. Upgrade all writer daemons; older writers do not annotate new terminal transitions.

recovery.detail: Existing legacy schedules require no recovery on upgrade. Newly published stop declarations survive restart and binary rollback; restoring a deliberately stopped duty requires explicit redeclaration. Rollback does not erase the stored epoch or source annotations.
